questions.prompt: Which state is the MOST compressible?
questions.explain: Gases have large spaces between particles, so they can be squashed easily.

questions.prompt: Sort each statement into the state it describes.
questions.explain: Forces are strongest and spaces smallest in solids; forces weakest and spaces largest in gases; liquids are in between.

questions.prompt: Why can a large volume of LPG be stored in a small cylinder?
options: Gases have large interparticle spaces, so they can be compressed
questions.explain: The large spaces between gas particles let us push them much closer together, so a lot of gas fits in a small space.

questions.prompt: When air in a syringe is compressed, what happens to the air particles?

feedback.0: Common mix-up! The particles stay the same size; the spaces between them shrink.

questions.explain: Compression reduces the spaces between particles. The particles themselves don't change size.

questions.prompt: A glass is filled to the brim with water. A spoon of sugar is stirred in and the water hardly overflows. What does this suggest?
options: There are spaces between water particles that sugar particles can fit into
questions.explain: The dissolved sugar particles fit into the spaces between the water particles, which is evidence for interparticle spaces.

questions.text: The forces of attraction between particles are ___ in solids and ___ in gases. Gases can be compressed because their interparticle spaces are ___.
questions.explain: Strongest in solids, weakest in gases; gases have large spaces.

questions.prompt: A syringe holds 60 mL of air. When pushed, the air is squeezed to half its volume. What is the new volume in mL?
questions.explain: Half of 60 mL is 30 mL. The same number of particles now have less space between them.

questions.prompt: Which of these use a COMPRESSED gas? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: LPG, oxygen cylinders and tyres all store gas squeezed into a smaller space.

questions.prompt: In the syringe lab, going from push force 0 to 20 squashes the gas a lot, but going from 80 to 100 squashes it only a little. Why?
options: As particles get closer together, there is less space left to remove
The gas turns into a solid
Gas particles get bigger when pushed
questions.explain: The more squashed the gas, the less empty space is left, so each extra push has a smaller effect.

questions.prompt: Explain why gases are compressible but liquids are not.
questions.modelAnswer: Gas particles are far apart with large interparticle spaces, so pushing can move them closer together. Liquid particles are already close together and touching, with very small spaces, so they can hardly be pushed any closer.
rubric: I said gases have large spaces between particles
I said liquid particles are close together / touching
I linked spaces to being able to push particles closer
questions.explain: Compressibility depends on how much empty space there is between particles.
